scope: Diagnose one native horizontal GTK2 reference arrow press in the authorized Domain/OS SR10.4 VM and determine whether the observed relative-counter path can be reproduced safely.

method.pointer: Existing R416 bounded Apollo relative-counter override path; host mouse remained uncaptured and MAME mouse option/device remained false/none.
method.press: One left-button field press for two emulated frame notifications after a fresh image confirmed the pointer over the left horizontal stepper cell.
method.observer: A frame notifier sampled :kbd:mouse1 read mask 16 while the press was held.
method.pixel_comparison: Native guest captures compared at 1:1; no scaling or registration adjustment.

target_before_press.visible: The pointer hotspot was inside the left horizontal stepper cell (the Trash Can is empty).

button_delivery.interpretation: The MAME input port reflected a short left-button press and returned to zero after release. This does not by itself prove the VUE widget accepted or acted on the event.

held_vs_released.interpretation: No visual transition was captured. The empty scrollbar may be at a disabled/end position; the direct field input route also does not yet prove VUE event handling.

counter_path_replay.result: The same starting counter values and recorded relative deltas did not reproduce the earlier visible pointer placement; the replay ended outside the arrow cell. No button was pressed in the replay.

cleanup.operation: Explicitly aborted at the non-target checkpoint; no additional press was sent.

result: The emulated button bit was observed high for two frames, but the VUE capture showed no pixel change between held and released states. The relative-counter route is not reproducible from identical reported starting values, so it is not a safe way to align the pointer after restoring the physical accumulator.
next: Keep GTK2 normal-state 15x15 comparisons R394/R401/R382. Do not change the GTK2 arrow recipe from this inconclusive hold test. Continue I167 by finding a verifiable input route on a scrollable VUE arrow or a reliable held-state capture; separate any MAME capture change from the saved profile and restore it immediately.
